sanskrit: aurdhvanabhasaḥ prathamaḥ sūryacetā uśadbhyaḥ | cakāra kṛtyām āsuraḥ sā no bhavatu bhadrayā ||
english: The first one, whose thought is of the sun, who rises toward the upper sky, who desires blessings — that Āsura fashioned a kṛtyā-sorcery; may it turn auspicious for us.

sanskrit: ya imāṃ kṛtyām upajahrur ye vā cakamire ?kṣitam | devānāṃ sarveṣāṃ svasā tān devī nirṛtir hanat ||
english: Those who brought this kṛtyā-sorcery, those who have desired the destruction — may the goddess Nirṛti, sister of all the gods, smite them.

sanskrit: kaśyapasya pratisaro dyauṣ pitā pṛthivī mātā | yathābhicakra devās tathāpi kṛṇutā punaḥ ||
english: This counter-amulet belongs to Kaśyapa; Heaven is the father, Earth is the mother. As the gods wrought the counter-spell, so do ye fashion it again.

sanskrit: yāḥ kṛtyā nīlavatīr yāḥ kṛtyāḥ pāśyāvatīḥ | kṛtyā yāś cakrur lohinīs tā ito nāśayāmasi ||
english: The kṛtyā-sorceries that are blue-tinged, the kṛtyā-sorceries that are noose-bearing, the kṛtyā-sorceries that those women made and that are blood-red — all of these we drive away from here.

sanskrit: yadi vā idam ājahrur ime bhadrā asann iti | kṛtyāsi kalyāṇy asi sāmuṃ kartāram anv ihi ||
english: Or if they brought this sorcery thinking "may these things be auspicious" — O kṛtyā, thou art benign, thou art propitious; go back and follow that very maker of thee.

sanskrit: bṛhat te varcaḥ prathatām upa dyāṃ mitrebhya edhi surabhiḥ suvarcāḥ | adhi te rājā varuṇo bravītu tasmā u tvaṃ haviṣā bhāgadhā asaḥ | śataṃ hemantān damayā sapatnān viśas tvā sarvā anu guṅgavo bhavantu ||
english: May thy great splendor spread upward to the sky; be thou fragrant and brilliant among thy allies. May King Varuṇa speak on thy behalf — and do thou share thy oblation with him. For a hundred winters subdue thy rivals; may all the clans follow thee with acclamation.

sanskrit: yas tvotpipānaṃ pratyutpipāti yas tvā sajāto viriphāty antitaḥ | indras taṃ yoktre adhame yunaktu tasmai (…) ||
english: He who rises up against thee as thou risest, he who is of thine own kin yet rails against thee from close by — may Indra bind him fast in the lowest tether; upon such a one [let the curse fall].

sanskrit: yas tvā yacchantaṃ pratiyaṃyamīti yas tvā jigīṣāt pṛtanāḥ samarye | bṛhaspatis tam ava jaṅghanītu tasmai (…) ||
english: He who restrains thee as thou art advancing, he who would conquer thy forces in the battle — may Bṛhaspati strike him down; upon such a one [let the curse fall].

sanskrit: ye te śulkam āharān ya u te baliṃ somaḥ sajātān upa saṃ namāti te | agniḥ sayugvān adhi te bravītu tasmai (…) ||
english: Those who have brought tribute to thee, and those who have brought thee their offering — Soma bends the men of thine own kin toward thee. May Agni, thy yokefellow, speak on thy behalf; upon such a one [let the curse fall].

sanskrit: variṣṭhaidhi puruḥ prajayā suvīro abhi pra yuṅkṣva damayā sapatnān | indro marutvān adhi te bravītu tasmā u tvaṃ haviṣā bhāgadhā asaḥ | śataṃ hemantān damayā sapatnān viśas tvā sarvā anu guṅgavo bhavantu ||
english: Be thou the greatest, abundant in offspring, possessed of good heroes; harness thyself forward, subdue thy rivals. May Indra with the Maruts speak on thy behalf — and do thou share thy oblation with him. For a hundred winters subdue thy rivals; may all the clans follow thee with acclamation.

sanskrit: bhagāya rājñe prathamaṃ juhomi viśve devā uttare mādayantām | uśan patnībhya uśatībhya ābhyaḥ patim agna ā vaha rātahavyaḥ ||
english: First I offer oblation to Bhaga the king; may all the gods rejoice in the latter portion. O Agni, thou who art richly offered oblation, desiring wives and these desiring women — bring to them a husband.

sanskrit: patiṃ vṛṇīṣva haviṣā gṛṇānā tam ā vahāt savitā taṃ te agniḥ | tasmai namasva śataśāradāya bhagabhaktā bhagavatī suvīrā ||
english: Choose thou a husband with oblation, praising him; may Savitṛ bring him, may Agni bring him to thee. Bow before him who shall live for a hundred autumns — thou who art endowed with good fortune, possessed of Bhaga's blessing, rich in brave sons.

sanskrit: yam aryaman patim asyai dideśitha jane cit santaṃ tam ihā vahāsi | sumaṅgaly apatighnī suśevā rāyaspoṣeṇa tam iṣā sacasva ||
english: The husband whom thou, O Aryaman, hast pointed out for her — even though he dwells among people — him thou shalt bring hither. O highly auspicious one, not a destroyer of husbands, benevolent — follow him with the abundance of wealth and with refreshment.

sanskrit: yaṃ te patim aryamā jāyamānāyai dhātā cakalpa tam ihā vahāsi | abhivareṇa haviṣā juhomi prajānann aitu sumanasyamānaḥ ||
english: The husband whom Aryaman and Dhātṛ ordained for thee at thy birth — him thou shalt bring hither. I offer oblation with the vow of choice; may he come knowing, coming with good will.

sanskrit: patiṃ te dyāvāpṛthivī adhātāṃ patiṃ mitrāvaruṇā vāto agniḥ | sapta rṣayo 'ditiḥ soma indras te tvā devāḥ pativatnīṃ kṛṇvantu ||
english: May Heaven and Earth bestow a husband upon thee, may Mitra and Varuṇa, Vāyu and Agni bestow a husband; may the seven Ṛṣis, Aditi, Soma, and Indra — may these gods make thee a woman possessed of a husband.
